qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dominant underground rock excavation installed base (>50% share in key underground drilling niches) with ~68% recurring aftermarket revenue (drilling consumables, spare parts, on-site service). High customer switching costs driven by extreme cost of mine downtime ($50k+/hr), proprietary telemetry/automation (Mobilaris, RCS), and specialized underground service technician networks. Sustained GAAP ROIC >20% (tangible ROIC ~35-45%) and ~20% operating margins confirm strong pricing power. Primary erosion risks: mining capex deferral cycles and commoditization of low-end surface consumables.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Global leader in underground mining equipment and rock drilling solutions with ~68% recurring aftermarket revenue (consumables, spare parts, services). Inherits Atlas Copco decentralized culture and Wallenberg governance. Insulated across all 5 macrotrends as miners automate and electrify to combat labor shortages and critical mineral demand. Fortress balance sheet with net debt/NI <0.6x and 14.8x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: critical minerals mining volume 2.5% + aftermarket CPI-plus pricing 2.0% + automation/electrification mix 2.5% - cyclical timing drag 0.5% + net repurchases 0.5%]
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 23.3% and tangible operating ROIC of 35-45%. Operating margins consistently ~19-22%. Free cash flow conversion normalized to 98-101% in 2024-2025. Aftermarket represents ~68% of sales, insulating cash generation from mining capex cycles.
